 Select Language! English English Indonesian IDR / USD: ---- As of: More Dasco: Asset seizure bill targets online gambling and crypto fraudster
 LM DH Lisa Monica, Ramdhani Pratama 19 November 2026, 15:10 WIB LM Lisa Monica Reporter DH Ramdhani Pratama Reporter WhatsApp Channel Parliament expands asset seizures to target financial and digital criminals. JAKARTA - The Asset Forfeiture Law relating to Corruption and Other Criminal Offences targets not only corruption offenders but also online gambling operators, crypto scammers, fraudulent investment schemes and fraudulent umrah travel agencies.
 Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives (DPR RI), Sufmi Dasco Ahmad, said the legislation, passed during a DPR RI plenary session on Thursday (19 November), has a broad scope, allowing the state to seize assets derived from various criminal offences.
 According to Dasco, the law serves as an instrument to deter criminals whose activities harm the public, particularly low-income groups who fall victim to online fraud and gambling.
 “(The Asset Forfeiture Law) is one way of deterring online gambling operators who are currently running their businesses and victimising ordinary people who gamble online,” Dasco said at the Parliament Complex in Senayan, Jakarta, on Thursday (19 November).
 Read Also: Foreign outflow reaches Rp855 billion, BBCA tops sell at Rp344 billion He added that assets belonging to crypto scammers, fraudulent investment operators, fraudulent umrah travel agencies and online gambling operators could all be subject to forfeiture.
 “For example, in cases involving crypto fraud, fraudulent investments, umrah travel scams and even online gambling operators, their assets can be seized under the Asset Forfeiture Law,” Dasco said.
 Dasco explained that assets derived from criminal activities could be traced, seized and managed by the Asset Forfeiture Proceeds Management Agency. The mechanism would also allow the state to pursue asset forfeiture when suspects or defendants flee overseas.
 “For example, if a defendant flees but their assets can still be seized, they can be seized immediately. In addition to corruption, the Asset Forfeiture Law also covers other criminal offences that cause considerable harm to the public,” he said.
 Six Categories of Crimes Beyond Corruption 
 Based on the discussions between the DPR and the government, the scope of criminal offences subject to asset forfeiture includes six categories of crimes beyond corruption.
 These include narcotics and psychotropic substances offences, terrorism and terrorism financing, human smuggling, the smuggling of weapons, ammunition and hazardous materials, human trafficking, as well as fraud and embezzlement involving information technology and/or affecting the wider public economy.
 The provisions concerning fraud and embezzlement also cover online gambling, investment fraud and crypto asset scams.
 The law establishes two asset forfeiture mechanisms: conviction-based forfeiture, which is based on a criminal court ruling, and non-conviction-based forfeiture, which does not require a criminal conviction against the offender.
 Under the second mechanism, asset forfeiture proceedings can continue in certain circumstances even when the offender cannot be brought before the court or prosecuted through criminal proceedings. However, the process must still follow legal procedures, including judicial review.
 The DPR has also included provisions for independent oversight, balanced evidentiary requirements and digital transparency to prevent the abuse of authority during asset forfeiture proceedings.
 Online Gambling Funds Reach IDR286.84 Trillion 
 The urgency of the legislation is underscored by the enormous volume of money circulating through online gambling activities. The Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (PPATK) recorded online gambling transactions worth IDR286.84 trillion throughout 2025, involving 422.1 million transactions.
 Although this represented a 20% decline from IDR359.81 trillion in 2024, the activity continued to involve millions of people. PPATK recorded approximately 12.3 million people making deposits into online gambling platforms throughout 2025.
 Online gambling deposits also reached IDR36.01 trillion, down from IDR51.3 trillion in the previous year. Digital payment channels, including QRIS, are increasingly being used to make deposits.
 Beyond online gambling, financial fraud has also become a concern for regulators. The Financial Services Authority (OJK), through its Task Force for the Eradication of Illegal Financial Activities (Satgas PASTI), received 3,170 complaints concerning illegal investments between 1 January and 31 July 2026.
 During the same period, the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre (IASC) received 637,055 reports of financial transaction fraud between its launch on 22 November 2024 and 31 July 2026.
 Through its handling of these reports, the IASC successfully froze approximately IDR724.1 billion in funds linked to fraud and returned IDR204.3 billion to victims. (DH/LM)
